title: Multimodal token-mix: latency vs cost exploratory notes (Sept 2027)
body:
PURPOSE:
Working notes for an internal collateral piece comparing latency and cost when inference requests contain mixed token types (text tokens interleaved with small image-embedding frames or dense visual tokens). Goal: concise experiment log + cheap ASCII charts we can paste into a slide or one-pager. Not a final benchmark — rough, reproducible, and focused on observability signals that matter for routing/SLAs.

SUMMARY FINDINGS (TL;DR):
- Mixed-token sessions increase p99 more than p50 compared to pure-text at same token-count; impact grows nonlinearly once >20% tokens are "dense" (vision) tokens.
- KV-cache hit-rate mitigates p50 strongly but has diminishing returns on p99 for interleaved multimodal flows.
- INT8 quant gives ~1.6x throughput on A100 for pure-text, but mixed token encoding/decoder overhead reduces that to ~1.3x effective for multimodal (extra CPU pre/post procs).
- Cost per 1k sessions rises faster than token-count when visual tokens present because effective GPU utilization drops (short bursts of heavy compute + lots of small RPCs).

EXPERIMENT NOTES:
- Models tested: redwood-2-m (fp16 baseline), redwood-2-m-int8 (quant), redwood-multimodal-lite (layout-optimized).
- Hardware: A100-80GB (hosted), H100-80GB (dedicated), small edge T4 used for smoke.
- Request shape: 1) Pure-text: 512 text tokens. 2) Mixed-10: 512 tokens where 10% (51) are dense image tokens. 3) Mixed-30: 512 tokens where 30% (154) are dense tokens. 4) Sessionized: conversation with 6 turns, average 85 tokens/turn, 15% dense.
- KV-cache: run with cache ON (prefix caching for text tokens only) and OFF. Cache hit rates recorded per-session.
- Batching: small-batch (batch_size 1–4) and medium-batch (8–16). Autoscaling disabled to observe single-pod behaviour.
- Observability signals collected: p50, p90, p99 latency (ms), tail-variance (p99-p50), GPU occupancy, effective tokens/sec, cost estimate (USD per 1k sessions based on runtime billing rates).

ASCII CHARTS (quick paste-ready):
1) p50 / p99 latency vs % dense tokens (redwood-2-m on A100, fp16, batch=4)
   %dense | p50(ms) | p99(ms) | p99-p50
   ----------------------------------
   0%     |  82     |  210    | 128
   10%    |  95     |  370    | 275
   20%    | 115     |  610    | 495
   30%    | 160     | 1000    | 840

   Small sparkline (p99 progression):
   0%   ▏██▏ 210
   10%  ▏█████▏ 370
   20%  ▏████████▏ 610
   30%  ▏████████████▏ 1000

2) Effective throughput (tokens/sec) vs mode (A100, batch=8):
   Mode           | tokens/s | relative
   ------------------------------------
   Pure-text fp16  |  42k    | 1.00x
   Mixed-10 fp16   |  30k    | 0.71x
   Mixed-30 fp16   |  18k    | 0.43x
   Pure-text int8  |  67k    | 1.60x
   Mixed-30 int8   |  24k    | 0.57x (overhead from pre/post CPU ops)

3) Cost per 1k sessions (approx; hosted list rates approximated)
   Scenario        | cost ($) | note
   ------------------------------------------
   Pure-text fp16  |  9.2     | baseline
   Mixed-10 fp16   | 11.9     | +29%
   Mixed-30 fp16   | 17.8     | +94%
   Pure-text int8  |  6.1     | quant savings
   Mixed-30 int8   | 12.5     | savings eroded by CPU work

OBSERVABILITY INSIGHTS (interpretation):
- Tail sensitivity: p99 increases sharply with token-type heterogeneity because short windows of heavy compute (dense token decode) create queuing/backpressure and increase scheduler jitter for other RPCs. This suggests SLOs and routing should be aware of token composition, not just token count.
- Cache utility: KV-cache reduces p50 substantially for sessionized text, but provides marginal p99 improvement for mixed flows because dense tokens are not cacheable in our current scheme.
- Quantization trade: INT8 helps but operational overhead (additional CPU serialization/deserialization for multimodal frames) reduces theoretical gains. For dedicated deployments with fewer network hops and colocated preproc, int8 becomes more attractive.
- Batching: larger batches help throughput but worsen p99 for mixed sessions (longer head-of-line blocking). For multimodal, opportunistic small windows with elastic preemption perform better for tails.

REPRODUCIBILITY (short recipe):
- Use workload generator: tools/mm-workgen:v0.3 (script attached in linked PR). Config: --model redwood-2-m --hw a100 --batch 4 --seq 512 --dense-pct 20 --sessionize 6 --kvcache on/off --quant fp16|int8
- Collect traces with obs-agent v2: tags session_id, dense_pct, kv_cache, quant, batch_size, pod_id.
- Store results as CSV: columns=run,model,hw,batch,seq,dense_pct,kv_cache,quant,p50,p90,p99,tokens_s, gpu_occ,cost_1k

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- How to best label token composition at the API layer so routing/policy can use it without leaking PII? (privacy/legal check)
- Small-image vs long-image distinction: our "dense token" prototype lumps several vision token types. Need finer bucketization (thumbnail vs full embedding).
- Investigate colocated pre/postproc on same pod (reduce CPU network overhead) — measure again for int8 workloads. (Affects Dedicated/Private product messaging).
- Quick follow-up experiment: H100 80GB, batch 4, mixed-15, with colocated preproc. Hypothesis: int8 wins back 1.4x and p99 reduces ~15%.

NOTES FOR CUSTOMER-FACING SLIDE (one-liners):
- "Multimodal sessions behave like bursty compute: p99 climbs nonlinearly with the fraction of dense tokens — route or price accordingly."
- "KV-cache buys latency for conversational text, but doesn’t help dense visual frames today; consider per-token-type caching metrics."
- "Quantization saves money, but operational cost depends on where image pre/post-processing runs."

LINKS/REFERENCES:
- Experiment harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mm-workgen (see run/configs/mixed-2027-sept.yaml)
- Related ticket: OBS-3421 (measure multimodal p99 anomalies)
- Runtime PR for trace tags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2783

ACTION ITEMS (owner tags):
- Priya: draft short slide (2 slides) summarizing charts + suggested routing policy (due 2027-10-05).
- Ethan: run H100 colocated-preproc experiment (target 2027-09-30) and upload CSV.
- Laura: add token-composition field proposal to API design doc and loop privacy (due 2027-10-08).
- Miguel: verify cost calc assumptions against billing team and update cost numbers if necessary (2027-10-06).

END (working draft)

-- Priya Rao (eng-observability)
